name: templet
description: Emmet-style abbreviations that compose template-language keywords, plain Emmet and your own snippets in one expression.

templet.snippets.markdownDescription: Named snippets usable as abbreviation segments. Keys are names, values are snippet bodies with `\t` indentation and `${1:placeholder}` tabstops. A snippet name shadows the built-in Emmet snippet of the same name.

templet.keywords.markdownDescription: Template-language keywords, keyed by dialect then keyword name. Merged over the built-in dialects, so you can add keywords or override built-in ones. Each keyword is `{ "open": "…", "close": "…", "defaultArg": "…", "branch": false }`. Use `${arg}` in `open` for the keyword argument, and write a literal dollar sign as `\$`.

open.description: Opening tag. May contain ${arg} and snippet tabstops.

close.description: Closing tag. Empty for branch keywords.

defaultArg.description: Placeholder used when the abbreviation gives no argument.

branch.description: True for keywords like else/elsif that continue an enclosing block instead of opening their own.

templet.languages.markdownDescription: Maps a VS Code language id to a Templet dialect, e.g. `{ "html": "twig" }`. Merged over the built-in mapping.

templet.preview.description: Show a live preview of the expansion while typing in the abbreviation input box.

templet.suggest.description: Suggest the expansion of the abbreviation before the cursor as you type, previewing the result in the suggestion details.

templet.inlinePreview.markdownDescription: Preview the expansion as ghost text in the editor while you type, accepted with `Tab`. VS Code hides inline suggestions while the suggestion list is open, so turn off `#templet.suggest#` to leave only the ghost text.

templet.suggestPlainEmmet.markdownDescription: Also suggest abbreviations that use no keyword and no Templet snippet. Off by default because VS Code's built-in Emmet already offers those wherever `#emmet.includeLanguages#` maps your language to HTML; turn it on if you have not configured that.

templet.configFile.description: Workspace-relative file holding project-specific keywords, snippets and language mappings. Values here win over user settings.

scripts.test: npm run compile && cd out && node --test
